NiSource Internship Program Introduction

NiSource is currently seeking a Summer Engineering Intern. Successful applicants will become integral members of the department while learning within a team environment, completing meaningful tasks and collaborating with team members and leaders on important projects. This position will be a great opportunity for the candidate desiring to launch their career in the field. Successful applicants will build professional relationships with other interns and all levels of NiSource personnel while participating in rewarding professional development exercises and fun, team-building activities. Interns will obtain a broad overview of NiSource's operations and current events in the utilities industry.

This is a 12-week summer internship program starting in May 2027, for students entering their junior or senior year in fall 2027. The role is based in Valparaiso, IN. Candidates must reside within 50 miles of the reporting location to be eligible.

Job Summary
NiSource is currently seeking Summer Engineering Interns at our IN locations. Successful applicants will become integral members of the department while learning within a team environment, completing meaningful tasks and collaborating with team members and leaders on important projects. These positions will be a great opportunity for the candidate desiring to launch their career in the Engineering field. Successful applicants will build professional relationships with other interns and all levels of NiSource personnel while participating in rewarding professional development exercises and fun, team-building activities. Interns will obtain a broad overview of NiSource's operations and current events in the utilities industry.

Essential Functions

- Work within a highly effective team managing the Chemical & Environmental Compliance Program for all Generating Stations
- Support data collection and reporting to stakeholders around Station Chemical & Environmental performance
- Promote continuous improvement within the department through data analysis and collaboration
- Assist in the organization and generation of reports for Compliance purposes
- Assist in the monitoring of plant chemical and mechanical systems / equipment to ensure compliance
- Evaluate trends of operating data, preventive testing, and corrective maintenance performance to identify problem areas
- Support department Capital and O&M projects for new or existing Process Chemistry / Environmental equipment
- Successful candidate to start in summer session

Required Qualifications for Position

- Current student of an accredited college/university pursuing a four-year degree in Chemistry, Environmental Science, Engineering or Technology.
- Must have completed at least one year of undergraduate study
- Ability to work 40 hrs/week during the summer
- Must have a valid driver's license
- Proficiency with PC applications and prefer strong skills with MS Excel & Access
- Proven communication skills
- Good written and oral communication skills.
- Good planning, organizational, verbal, and written communication skills.
- Ability to perform duties effectively at all times.
- GPA 3.0 and above
- Authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship
- DL NUMBER - Driver License, Valid and in State Must have a valid driver's license Upon Hire

The Role

We are excited to offer an internship opportunity for a talented student to join the data science team at Schonfeld. The data science team is responsible for creating Schonfeld's proprietary curated and feature datasets, conducting data analytics and research, and ultimately add value to various investment strategies.

What You’ll Do

As a data scientist, you will work closely with the engineering teams to optimize data ingestion pipelines, ensuring high-quality data input. You will also collaborate with portfolio manager teams to extract insights from data and systematically generate features or signals that feed into the alpha generation process. Additionally, you will develop domain expertise across various financial asset classes and datasets, produce curated datasets to standardize research, conduct quantitative analysis to generate ideas and validate hypothesis through backtesting. The ideal candidate will possess both a passion for data science disciplines and a strong interest in financial markets.

What You’ll Bring

What you need:

- Knowledge of Python, SQL, or other programming languages

- Proficiency with statistical and machine learning packages for quantitative analysis

- Experience researching and analyzing financial datasets

- Attention to detail and strong communication skills

- Degree in quantitative field such as computer science, data science or financial engineering

We’d love if you had:

- Strong passion for financial markets and related datasets

- Knowledge of deep learning models

- Familiarity with AI tools to accelerate work, with a focus on adding analysis and insight

- Experience with any of the following technologies: Spark, Kafka, Docker, Airflow

- Knowledge of financial asset classes such as equity, futures, and fixed Income

Our Internship

Kick-start your career in finance with the Schonfeld Summer Internship! Over the course of 10 action-packed weeks, you will have the opportunity to build solutions that tackle real-world challenges and leave a lasting impact on the firm. As an intern, you’ll join a close-knit team that is ready to support your growth and accelerate your career. We will pair you with a dedicated manager and a mentor who’ll guide your development over the course of the internship and beyond. Throughout the program, you will have the chance to connect with senior leaders through a series of learning sessions, attend hands-on skills workshops, network at social events and get a behind-the-scenes look at how various functions power the firm. We’ll empower you to bring your ideas to life and make an impact.

Who We Are

Schonfeld is a global multi-manager hedge fund that strives to deliver industry-leading risk-adjusted returns for our investors. We leverage both internal and external portfolio manager teams around the world, seeking to capitalize on inefficiencies and opportunities within the markets. We draw from decades of experience and a significant investment in proprietary technology, infrastructure and risk analytics to invest across four main strategies: Quant, Tactical, Fundamental Equity and Discretionary Macro & Fixed Income.

Our Culture

At Schonfeld, we’ll invest in you. Attracting and retaining top talent is at the heart of what we do, because we believe that exceptional outcomes begin with exceptional people. We foster a culture where talent is empowered to continually learn, innovate and pursue ambitious goals. We are teamwork-oriented, collaborative and encourage ideas—at all levels—to be shared. As an organization committed to investing in our people, we provide learning and educational offerings and opportunities to make an impact. We encourage community through internal networks, external partnerships and service initiatives that promote inclusion and purpose beyond the firm’s walls.

The annual base pay for this role is expected to be between $100,000 and $110,000 which will be prorated based on internship start and end date. The expected base pay range is based on information at the time this post was generated. Actual compensation for the successful candidate will be determined based on a variety of factors such as skills, qualifications and experience and level of education.

Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

At Micron, we are driving the future of memory technology through innovative DRAM solutions that power artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and next-generation applications. The Thin Films Process Development Engineering team develops and optimizes advanced thin film deposition and metallization processes that enable future memory scaling and improved device performance. Our engineers collaborate across process, integration, equipment, metrology, and product engineering fields to solve complex manufacturing challenges and advance innovative semiconductor technologies.

As an intern focused on developing thin films processes, you will gain hands-on experience developing and characterizing advanced thin film and metallization processes used in DRAM manufacturing. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will play a role in a technical project dedicated to process development, data analysis, process optimization, and technology innovation. Interns will contribute to the development of advanced metallization and thin-film processes supporting ground-breaking DRAM technologies. Projects may include deposition process development, process characterization, tool qualification, materials evaluation, defect reduction, AI-Enabled data analysis, and process optimization for advanced memory devices. This internship provides exposure to semiconductor manufacturing, cleanroom operations, and advanced engineering methodologies while supporting real-world technology development initiatives.

Responsibilities

- Support the development, optimization, and characterization of advanced thin film deposition and metallization processes for next-generation DRAM technologies.
- Design and implement experiments using Design of Experiments (DOE) methodologies and perform statistical analysis to evaluate process performance and drive improvements.
- Collect, analyze, and visualize process and metrology data to identify trends, process interactions, and engineering opportunities.
- Collaborate with process, integration, equipment, metrology, and product engineering teams to investigate process excursions, perform root-cause analysis, and support technology development activities.
- Develop and utilize AI-Assisted workflows, AI-Enabled engineering tools, automation solutions, or data analytics methods to improve process monitoring, technical reporting, engineering productivity, and decision-making.

Minimum Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s degree in Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, or a related engineering or technical field.
- Experience with experimental design, data analysis, statistical methods, or engineering research projects.
- Knowledge of materials characterization, semiconductor processing, thin films, or related manufacturing technologies.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, written, and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and collaborate effectively in a team environment.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with semiconductor process development, deposition technologies, metallization processes, or advanced manufacturing environments.
- Experience with programming, scripting, automation, data science, or Leveraging AI to support engineering analysis and workflow optimization.
- Familiarity with statistical software, data visualization tools, Python, JMP, MATLAB, R, or similar analytical platforms.
- Experience interpreting metrology and characterization data to evaluate material properties, process capability, or manufacturing performance.
- Demonstrated ability to communicate technical findings and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Job Description:

The Internship Program is a full time 10-week program focused on providing college students with practical business experience. It allows participants to develop leadership skills, broaden their understanding of the concepts learned in school and "get a taste of the real world" before they are fully committed to it.

Position is available at El Paso, TX/Juarez, MX​ supporting the MedTech Supply Chain business. Specific responsibilities may include budget support, capital budgeting, financial consolidation, and analysis, and/or ad-hoc projects. Other common tasks include analysis of financial questions and problems, problem solving, active business partnering and developing innovative methods to improve job metrics and processes.

The Intern program is one of the primary sources of talent for entrance into Johnson & Johnson's Finance Leadership Development Program (FLDP). The Finance Leadership Development Program (FLDP) is a two-and-a-half-year program designed specifically to prepare and develop future generations of business leaders within the finance organization. Participants will develop critical leadership & technical skills through rotational assignments at J&J business units, in-depth training, & ongoing coaching and feedback. FLDP participants complete 2 rotations, first being ~18 months followed by a 12-month rotation. These rotational assignments are supplemented by five weeks of various trainings over the course of the program taught and led by internal & external resources. Training courses provide overviews of the various functions within J&J and follow a robust and interactive curriculum that helps develop FLDP participants on key competencies such as problem-solving/analysis, technical skills, business knowledge, teamwork, and leadership. Dual U.S. and Mexican Citizenship is required.

Qualifications

- Current enrollment in an accredited College/University is required pursuing an undergraduate or Fifth Year Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Data Analytics or business-related major with an expected graduation date in 2028 or 2029.
- A minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA is required.
- Intermediate knowledge of MS Excel is preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to rapidly learn, evaluate, and adopt new AI tools and ways of working to meet evolving business needs.
- Legal Authorization to work in the United States, without requiring sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g. H1-B status) now or in the future is required.
- Dual U.S. and Mexican Citizenship is required.

Eligible applicants will be reviewed in the early fall 2026 timeframe.
